jordan: Quick AH follow-up re: runway + procurement notes. Two quick asks: 1) if a team finds a vendor that could cut inference cost but needs a 3mo prepay, what's the fastest path to get approval? 2) Any immediate hiring spend freezes we should know about?

kevin (Eng): Re: vendor prepay - we have a potential GPU spot reseller who wants 3mo prepay for a 20% discount. Need to know who signs and whether we can do a partial prepay on a P-card.

maria (CFO): Short: prepay > $10k must go through Procurement + Finance Ops. P-card is not for prepay commitments. For a 3mo prepay, route through FIN-300 intake (procurement form) and tag it as "cost optimization". Procurement will evaluate SLA, refund/exit terms, and counterparty risk.

jordan: who is the intake owner for FIN-300?

dylan (Finance Ops): I own FIN-300 triage. Please include expected savings %, break-even, and whether this is a committed capacity vs reseller credit. Template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-300. We'll aim for a 48-72hr turnaround if the vendor is known and low-risk.

harper: For clarity, is "prepay" always capitalized as Opex vs Capex? need to update budget trackers.

maria (CFO): Good catch. We treat prepaid service commitments as Opex when they are less than 12 months and don't transfer an asset to Redwood. If it's effectively buying hardware or a transferable asset, classify as CapEx and loop in FP&A.

ops-team: Any guidance on emergency exceptions for prod-level tooling that we must buy immediately?

maria (CFO): Emergency purchases still need post-hoc documentation. For < $2k we can triage after purchase (P-card ok). For $2k-$10k, notify Finance Ops before purchase; Procurement will expedite. > $10k follow standard intake. Document must include impact statement and approver's name.

kevin (Eng): If a cost optimization trade reduces unit cost but adds a 3mo cash hit, will that show up in the runway calc that triggers hiring holds?

sam (CEO): High level: we look at multi-month commitments in runway modeling. Short-term cash usage for material unit cost improvements is allowed if the net effect improves 12mo runway and product velocity. But any > $50k cash commitment needs Exec review.

maria (CFO): Adding nuance: our runway projection uses trailing cash + committed outflows. So yes, prepay reduces available runway immediately. That's why we require the FIN-300 with ROI and a cash-flow projection.

jordan: Action list: 1) teams to file FIN-300 for any prepay/commitment > $2k, 2) tag Finance Ops w/ expected savings and cash impact, 3) Procurement will flag legal/Security if vendor touches data.

procure-bot: Created FIN-300-7: "3mo prepay inquiry - infra cost optimization" assigned to dylan.

kevin (Eng): Thanks all. We'll run the numbers and submit the FIN-300. Appreciate the 72hr target.

dylan (Finance Ops): Quick note for submitters: include two scenarios in the form: conservative (60% utilization) and aggressive (90% utilization) so Procurement can model break-even. Also include cancellation windows.

maria (CFO): Final: No company-wide hiring freeze announced today. We will institute role-by-role pause if runway modeling deteriorates. Continue to route headcount asks through People Ops + Hiring Committee as usual.

jordan: perfect, thanks everyone. I'll post the summary in the infra channel and link the FIN-300 ticket once submitted. :thumbsup:
